_about: Ask Ethicare's official-source settings (12 Oct 2026). 'domains' = what counts as an official site: links to these from the guides are collected into the index, and live look-ups are limited to 'search' only. 'facts' = short, checked extracts from official pages, each with its link and the date it was checked. Add Sophie's full website list to 'search' and 'domains'. Review every fact by its 'checked' date.

facts.topic: age limit australia visa 482 skills in demand work visa
facts.text: The Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) has no age limit.
facts.source: Smart Move Australia (Australian Government), Skills in Demand visa

facts.topic: age limit australia permanent residence 186 employer nomination scheme under 45 pr permanent residency resident
facts.text: The Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186) generally requires the applicant to be under 45 when they apply, with some exemptions. Home Affairs sets out the exemptions on its subclass 186 pages.
facts.source: Department of Home Affairs, Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186)

facts.topic: age limit new zealand accredited employer work visa aewv
facts.text: Immigration New Zealand's Accredited Employer Work Visa page states no age requirement. Police certificates are needed from age 17 if the person's total time in New Zealand will be 24 months or more.
facts.source: Immigration New Zealand, Accredited Employer Work Visa

facts.topic: age limit new zealand green list straight to residence tier 1 pr permanent residency resident
facts.text: Straight to Residence Visa: "You must be aged 55 or younger when you apply."
facts.source: Immigration New Zealand, Straight to Residence Visa

facts.topic: age limit new zealand green list work to residence tier 2 pr permanent residency resident
facts.text: Work to Residence Visa: "You must be aged 55 or younger when you apply."
facts.source: Immigration New Zealand, Work to Residence Visa

facts.topic: age limit new zealand skilled migrant category residence pr permanent residency resident
facts.text: Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa: "You must be aged 55 or younger when you apply."
facts.source: Immigration New Zealand, Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa

facts.topic: ahpra english language test scores change april 2026
facts.text: From 23 April 2026, the National Boards updated the minimum scores of accepted English tests. Tests taken on or before 22 April 2026 are judged against the older scores; tests taken on or after 23 April 2026 against the new ones.
facts.source: Ahpra, Accepted English language tests

facts.topic: police certificate fingerprints fingerprinting new zealand visa character
facts.text: Immigration New Zealand: some issuing authorities "may require a set of fingerprints when you request a police certificate." Private fingerprinting businesses operate in many areas of New Zealand; NZ Police only offer the service in some regions and on specific days. Bring a passport or other photo ID.
facts.source: Immigration New Zealand, Police certificates; NZ Police, having fingerprints taken

facts.topic: police certificate new zealand visa 24 months stay who needs
facts.text: Immigration New Zealand: whether you need a police certificate depends on the visa and how long you plan to stay; for stays of 24 months or longer you must provide one with your application. Its 'How to get a police certificate' tool shows the process for each country.
facts.source: Immigration New Zealand, Police certificates

facts.topic: police certificate how old valid six 6 months new zealand visa timing expiry
facts.text: Immigration New Zealand: a police certificate must be "less than 6 months old when you submit your visa application", and INZ may ask for a further certificate if the first becomes a year old from its date of issue before a decision is made.
facts.source: Immigration New Zealand, How to get a police certificate

facts.topic: 1737 need to talk mental health crisis counsellor text call new zealand nz support struggling low depressed depression anxious anxiety lonely homesick suicidal suicide down overwhelmed stressed stress cope coping distress self harm unsafe
facts.text: In New Zealand you can "text or call 1737 anytime to connect with a trained counsellor or peer support worker." It is "a free, confidential helpline in New Zealand". Counsellors are available 24/7, and peer support is available daily from 2pm to 10pm, by phone only.
facts.source: 1737, How 1737 Works

facts.topic: healthline nurse advice phone free 24 hours new zealand nz sick unwell interpreter struggling low depressed depression anxious anxiety lonely homesick suicidal suicide down overwhelmed stressed stress cope coping distress self harm unsafe
facts.text: "Call Healthline on 0800 611 116 for free, for advice from our trained registered nurses." Nurses are available "any time - 24 hours a day, 7 days a week", "Phone calls are free from within New Zealand – this includes calls from a mobile phone", and "If you need to talk to someone in your own language, Healthline can arrange an interpreter."
facts.source: Ministry of Health (Manatū Hauora), Healthline

facts.topic: emergency 111 police fire ambulance new zealand nz
facts.text: In New Zealand, call 111 when you need an emergency response from Police, Fire or Ambulance. The page says "111 calls are free", and you can call from a mobile phone even if you have no credit. If you are not sure whether it is an emergency, call 111 and the operator will help you decide.
facts.source: New Zealand Police, 111 Emergency Services

facts.topic: lifeline crisis support suicide australia 13 11 14 text chat struggling low depressed depression anxious anxiety lonely homesick suicidal suicide down overwhelmed stressed stress cope coping distress self harm unsafe
facts.text: "Lifeline's 13 11 14 crisis support service is available 24/7" and "The Lifeline phone service is available 24/7, to anyone in Australia." You can also text 0477 13 11 14 or use online chat. "If life is in danger, call Triple Zero (000)."
facts.source: Lifeline Australia, Lifeline crisis support - 13 11 14

facts.topic: 13yarn aboriginal torres strait islander crisis support australia yarn struggling low depressed depression anxious anxiety lonely homesick suicidal suicide down overwhelmed stressed stress cope coping distress self harm unsafe
facts.text: "13YARN is the first national service of its kind for Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander people in crisis." Call 13YARN (13 92 76). It is "Available 24/7 across Australia from any phone" and calls are free and confidential. "If life is in danger call 000."
facts.source: 13YARN, Home

facts.topic: interpreter translating tis national language australia 131 450 free
facts.text: TIS National's immediate phone interpreting is "available 24 hours a day, every day of the year by calling 131 450." "The majority of TIS National interpreting services are free to non-English speakers", although calls from mobiles or from outside Australia may cost more, depending on your provider.
facts.source: TIS National (Department of Home Affairs), Interpreting services for non-English speakers

facts.topic: emergency triple zero 000 police fire ambulance australia
facts.text: In Australia, call Triple Zero (000) if someone is seriously injured or needs urgent medical help, if a life or property is threatened, or if you have just seen a serious accident or crime. "Triple Zero calls are free." The operator will ask "Do you want Police, Fire or Ambulance?"
facts.source: Triple Zero (Australian Government), Home

facts.topic: reciprocal health care agreement australia medicare countries uk ireland new zealand which countries
facts.text: "As at 1 February 2024, Australia has Reciprocal Health Care Agreements with the following countries": Belgium, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Malta, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Slovenia, Sweden and the United Kingdom. Cover for visitors from Italy and Malta is limited to 6 months from arrival. "Reciprocal Health Care Agreements do not cover the cost of treatment as a private patient in a public or private hospital."
facts.source: Australian Government Department of Health, Note GN.3.9, Medicare Benefits Schedule

facts.topic: reciprocal health care ireland new zealand australia hospital only no gp
facts.text: "Visitors from New Zealand and Ireland are entitled to public hospital care and PBS drugs only (not MBS services)." This means GP and other out-of-hospital Medicare services are not covered for them under the agreement.
facts.source: Australian Government Department of Health, Note GN.3.9, Medicare Benefits Schedule

facts.topic: reciprocal health care uk united kingdom medicare australia enrol arrival british
facts.text: To use the UK agreement in Australia, "you must have been living in the United Kingdom (UK) before arriving in Australia." It covers medically necessary care outside hospital, "medically necessary care as a public patient in a public hospital including inpatient and outpatient services", and some PBS medicines at the general rate. You enrol through myGov or with a Medicare enrolment form. You need your current visa, your passport, and proof of UK residence, such as a UK GHIC, an EHIC marked "UK", or two dated documents such as a lease, bank statement or utility account.
facts.source: Services Australia, Reciprocal Health Care Agreements - visiting from the United Kingdom

facts.topic: reciprocal health care new zealand nz citizen visiting australia medicare hospital
facts.text: New Zealand visitors must be "a New Zealand citizen or resident of New Zealand before arriving in Australia" and "temporarily visiting Australia." "Your cover is for public inpatient and outpatient hospital care only". Visits to a doctor do not count as outpatient care.
facts.source: Services Australia, Reciprocal Health Care Agreements - visiting from New Zealand

facts.topic: new zealand nz public healthcare eligibility work visa two years free hospital gp eligible
facts.text: In New Zealand you get the same publicly funded medical treatment as New Zealanders if you are "in NZ on a work visa that's valid for 2 years or more" (the visa starts on "your first day in NZ"). Australian citizens and permanent residents who have lived, or intend to live, in NZ for 2 years or more are also eligible. Otherwise "you'll need to pay for all your medical care", although ACC gives "comprehensive, no-fault personal injury cover for all NZ residents and visitors."
facts.source: New Zealand Government (govt.nz), Healthcare if you're in NZ on a work visa

facts.topic: asms union senior doctors dentists consultants specialists new zealand pay
facts.text: ASMS says: "We are the union for senior salaried doctors and dentists." It covers professional issues and employment matters, including collective agreements.
facts.source: Association of Salaried Medical Specialists (ASMS), About Us

facts.topic: psa union allied health psychologist social worker occupational therapist new zealand pay
facts.text: PSA calls itself "Aotearoa New Zealand's largest trade union", representing "more than 95,000 workers". It says "THE PSA IS THE UNION FOR ALLIED HEALTH", and "People working in more than 120 professions are covered including social workers." Its member stories include clinical psychologists and occupational therapists.
facts.source: New Zealand Public Service Association (PSA), Allied

facts.topic: nzno nurses union new zealand nurses organisation midwives pay
facts.text: NZNO is "The New Zealand Nurses Organisation Tōpūtanga Tapuhi Kaitiaki o Aotearoa (NZNO)." Its chief executive says: "We are more than 55,000 strong and growing."
facts.source: NZNO, media release: NZNO promises to 'go hard' for nursing with new campaign

facts.topic: sorted money budgeting new zealand nz free government financial guidance
facts.text: "Sorted's a free service run by Te Ara Ahunga Ora Retirement Commission", which is "the government-funded, independent agency dedicated to helping New Zealanders get ahead financially." "We're not here to sell you anything."
facts.source: Sorted, All about us

facts.topic: moneysmart money budgeting australia free government asic
facts.text: Moneysmart is "a Federal Government website, brought to you by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC)", offering "free tools, tips and guidance."
facts.source: Moneysmart (ASIC), About us

facts.topic: kiwisaver pension retirement savings new zealand work visa eligible join
facts.text: You can join KiwiSaver if you are "a New Zealand citizen, or entitled to live in New Zealand indefinitely" and you "live or normally live in New Zealand." "You cannot join KiwiSaver if you have a temporary, visitor, work or student visa." If you are eligible, "your employer might automatically enrol you into KiwiSaver" when you start a new job.
facts.source: Inland Revenue (IRD), Joining KiwiSaver

facts.topic: superannuation super australia temporary resident visa employer dasp leaving
facts.text: Your employer "may be required to make super contributions to a super fund on your behalf". "Generally, this does not depend on your visa (so long as you have work rights)." If you leave after working on a temporary visa, "you may be eligible to claim your super (less tax) as a Departing Australia superannuation payment (DASP)". However, "You can only submit a DASP claim after you have left Australia and your visa has expired."
facts.source: Australian Taxation Office, How superannuation applies to temporary residents

facts.topic: uk state pension abroad frozen annual increase new zealand national insurance voluntary
facts.text: "Your State Pension will only increase each year if you live in" the EEA, Gibraltar, Switzerland or a country with a social security agreement with the UK. You "cannot get increases in Canada or New Zealand." "You will not get yearly increases if you live outside these countries." "You might be able to pay voluntary contributions to fill in gaps in your National Insurance record."
facts.source: GOV.UK, State Pension if you retire abroad: How your pension is affected

facts.topic: uk state pension claim abroad international pension centre
facts.text: To claim the UK State Pension while living abroad, "You must be within 4 months of your State Pension age to claim." You can contact the International Pension Centre or send it the international claim form.
facts.source: GOV.UK, State Pension if you retire abroad: Claim State Pension abroad

facts.topic: MCNZ COPS certificate of professional status good standing how recent doctor New Zealand
facts.text: The Medical Council of New Zealand says: "All COPS must be dated within 3 months of the date you will start practising in New Zealand." Letters of standing follow the same rule: "The letter must be dated within 3 months of the date you will start practising in New Zealand."
facts.source: Medical Council of New Zealand, Certificate of professional status (COPS)

facts.topic: MRTB medical radiation technologist radiographer radiation therapist letter good standing how recent New Zealand
facts.text: The Medical Radiation Technologists Board says you need "a Letter of good standing from each authority you've been registered with" and "The certificate must not be more than six months old at the date of your application."
facts.source: Medical Radiation Technologists Board, Internationally qualified registration

facts.topic: physiotherapy physio board certificate good standing COGS police certificate how recent New Zealand
facts.text: On the International General Pathway, the Physiotherapy Board says the Certificate of Good Standing (and the police certificate): "Document must be less than three months old on the date you submit your application." The International Express Pathway page gives the same rule: "Document must be less than 3 months old on the date you submit your application."
facts.source: Physiotherapy Board of New Zealand, International General Pathway

facts.topic: Ahpra certificate good standing registration status how recent Australia medical radiation practice all boards
facts.text: Ahpra says you must arrange "a Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Registration Status from the registration authority" in each jurisdiction where you are or were registered. "These certificates must be provided to us directly from the overseas regulator" and must be "dated within three months of your application being received."
facts.source: Ahpra, Information for international practitioners

facts.topic: Ahpra English test IELTS OET results how recent two years combine sittings Australia
facts.text: Under the English language skills registration standard, test results are accepted if obtained "within the two years before the date you lodge your application for registration", from "one test sitting, or a maximum of two test sittings in a 12-month period", and "Results from different test providers cannot be combined." The standard covers most National Boards, including medical, medical radiation practice, physiotherapy, occupational therapy and psychology. Nursing and midwifery has its own standard.
facts.source: Ahpra, English language skills registration standard

facts.topic: MCNZ English language test IELTS OET how recent two years doctor UK graduate exemption New Zealand
facts.text: The MCNZ English language policy says IELTS and OET results for doctors applying for registration are valid for "2 years of an application for registration." Graduates of medical schools in the UK, Ireland and certain other countries who "Speak English as a first language" can meet the requirement without a test (Option B).
facts.source: Medical Council of New Zealand, English language policy (PDF)

facts.topic: MRTB English IELTS OET how recent two years radiographer New Zealand
facts.text: The MRTB policy requires that "IELTS results were achieved within two (2)-years immediately prior to their registration application", although "In limited circumstances the test result may be more than two (2)-years prior to their application date." The policy sets no validity period for OET.
facts.source: Medical Radiation Technologists Board, Policy: English language proficiency August 2024 (PDF)

facts.topic: occupational therapy OT board English test IELTS OET how recent 24 months New Zealand
facts.text: The Occupational Therapy Board of New Zealand English language policy says: "Test results must be no older than 24 months when they are submitted."
facts.source: Occupational Therapy Board of New Zealand, English language policy for registration (PDF)

facts.topic: physiotherapy physio English test results how recent two years New Zealand
facts.text: The Physiotherapy Board says: "Test results must be less than 2 years old on the date you submit your application."
facts.source: Physiotherapy Board of New Zealand, English Proficiency Evidence (FAQ)

facts.topic: social work SWRB English test how recent two years IELTS online New Zealand
facts.text: The Social Workers Registration Board says: "The test must be completed within the two years immediately preceding an applicant commencing their application." IELTS Online results are not accepted.
facts.source: Social Workers Registration Board, Overseas qualifications

facts.topic: Immigration New Zealand residence English test results how recent two years skilled migrant
facts.text: For residence from work, Immigration New Zealand says "your result must be no more than 2 years old at the time you apply."
facts.source: Immigration New Zealand, English language test results for residence from work

facts.topic: Immigration New Zealand medical certificate chest x-ray how old three months visa
facts.text: Immigration New Zealand says: "Your chest X-ray and medical examination results must be no more than 3 months old when we get your application."
facts.source: Immigration New Zealand, How to get an X-ray or medical examination

facts.topic: Australia visa health examination medical results valid 12 months Home Affairs
facts.text: Home Affairs says: "The results of your health assessment are valid for 12 months from the time you completed your examinations." It adds that a health undertaking "will be valid for 6 months."
facts.source: Department of Home Affairs, After your health examinations

facts.topic: Australia skilled visa police certificate which countries 12 months 10 years
facts.text: For skilled visas, Home Affairs asks for police certificates "for every country where you've lived for 12 months in the past 10 years since turning 16." It also says "Health examination results are generally valid for 12 months."
facts.source: Department of Home Affairs, Applying for a skilled visa (Check twice, submit once)

facts.topic: New Zealand driving overseas licence 18 months 12 months 1 November 2026 convert NZTA
facts.text: NZTA says: "You can currently drive in New Zealand using an overseas car licence for up to 18 months from your last date of entry." and "From 1 November 2026, this reduces to 12 months." After that: "If you'll be in New Zealand longer than this, you'll need to convert your licence if you want to keep driving."
facts.source: NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi, Factsheet 72 Overseas driver licences (July 2026)

facts.topic: NSW driving overseas licence temporary visa six months permanent resident three months convert
facts.text: Temporary overseas visitors "can drive in NSW using your overseas licence for up to six months" and, if staying longer, "will need to obtain a NSW driver's licence within six months." Permanent residents can drive "up to three months from the date you arrive in Australia" and "must get a NSW licence within this three month period."
facts.source: NSW Government, Driving with an overseas or interstate licence in NSW

facts.topic: Victoria VicRoads driving overseas licence six months convert
facts.text: VicRoads says you can drive on an overseas licence if you "only plan to reside and drive in Victoria for less than 6 months", counted "from the day you start living in Victoria". "If you want to drive in Victoria for more than 6 months, you'll need to convert your overseas licence."
facts.source: VicRoads, Driving with your overseas licence in Victoria

facts.topic: Queensland driving overseas licence permanent visa three months transfer
facts.text: Permanent (resident) visa holders cannot drive on an overseas licence once they have "been living in Queensland for 3 months." Resident visas "don't include temporary, business or guardian visas", and the page gives no time limit for temporary visa holders.
facts.source: Queensland Government, Driving in Queensland on an interstate or overseas licence

facts.topic: Western Australia WA driving overseas licence permanent resident three months transfer
facts.text: For permanent residents and citizens moving to WA: "you can drive in Western Australia for up to 3 months using your overseas licence", and within that period "you will need to apply to transfer your overseas driver's licence to a WA driver's licence." No time limit is given for temporary visa holders.
facts.source: Department of Transport WA, Moving from overseas

facts.topic: South Australia SA driving overseas licence permanent resident 90 days three months
facts.text: SA.GOV.AU says: "If you become a permanent resident of South Australia, you must get your South Australian driver's licence within 90 days." My Licence SA puts it as "you have 3 months to get a South Australian driver's licence or permit." Neither page gives a time limit for visitors or temporary visa holders.
facts.source: SA.GOV.AU, Driving with your overseas licence in SA

facts.topic: Tasmania driving overseas licence temporary visa permanent visa six months conversion
facts.text: Transport Tasmania says you can drive on an overseas licence "if you are a visitor or have a temporary visa". For permanent visa holders, your "permanent visa has not been issued for longer than six months", or you are treated as unlicensed unless the Registrar approves an extension to the "six month conversion period".
facts.source: Transport Tasmania, Driving in Tasmania on an interstate or overseas licence

facts.topic: ACT Canberra driving overseas licence permanent visa three months temporary visa
facts.text: Access Canberra says permanent visa holders can "continue to use you overseas licence for 3 months" and then must "hold an ACT Driver Licence to drive in the ACT". Temporary visa holders who live in the ACT "may choose to obtain an ACT driver licence".
facts.source: Access Canberra, Drivers with licences from overseas

facts.topic: Northern Territory NT driving overseas licence three months transfer new resident
facts.text: NT.GOV.AU says "you can drive with your interstate or overseas licence for up to 3 months" and "If you remain in the NT for a continuous period of more than 3 months, you must transfer to an NT driver licence."
facts.source: NT.GOV.AU, Driving in the NT for new residents and visitors

facts.topic: NSW school fees 482 visa regional exemption Temporary Residents Program
facts.text: On the NSW Temporary Residents Program, "Most temporary resident students pay the temporary resident application fee and tuition fee". Since 1 January 2025, children on a 482 visa "may be eligible for exemption from the Temporary Residents Program tuition fee". To qualify, "The student and sponsored parent must reside in an eligible NSW regional postcode" and "The student must be enrolled and attend an eligible regional NSW government school". Also, "The exemption does not apply to the Temporary Residents Program application fee."
facts.source: NSW DE International, Fact sheet: Exemption for 482 visa in a regional school / Temporary Residents Program

facts.topic: Queensland QLD school fees 482 visa dependants exempt
facts.text: The Queensland schedule lists subclass 482 (Skills in Demand and Temporary Skill Shortage streams) with "Tuition fee payable" marked "No", and no Authority to Enrol or application fee is needed. This applies where the visa is "Held by the student or their parent and the student is listed as a dependent of that visa."
facts.source: Queensland Department of Education International, Schedule of visa subclasses and enrolment conditions

facts.topic: Western Australia WA school fees 482 visa family tuition fee
facts.text: "457 and 482 visa holders have a local enrolment entitlement." "They pay a family tuition fee of $4 000 per year" "regardless of the number of Pre-primary to Year 12 children enrolled at a public school." "No family tuition fee is payable if the oldest child is in Kindergarten."
facts.source: WA Department of Education, Enrolment Framework for Students with a Visa in Public Schools

facts.topic: South Australia SA school fees 482 visa income threshold Adelaide
facts.text: Families pay the student fee if "you're on a 482 visa", "your child or children attend government schools in the greater Adelaide region" and "your family's total income is over $78,000 per year (before tax)." The page gives a 2027 maximum of $7,000 per primary student and $8,200 per high school student.
facts.source: SA Department for Education, Student fees and enrolment in school for subclass 482 visa holders

facts.topic: Tasmania TAS school fees 482 visa Temporary Resident Program
facts.text: The Tasmanian table lists subclass 482 Temporary Skill Shortage with "TRP TUITION FEES PAYABLE?" marked "No". It also marks "APPLICATION FEE PAYABLE?" and "SCHOOL LEVIES PAYABLE?" as "Yes".
facts.source: DECYP / Tasmanian Government Education International, Temporary Resident Program (TRP) Visas at a Glance

facts.topic: ACT Canberra school fees 482 visa fee exemption
facts.text: Subclass 482 ("Skills in demand") is not on the ACT list of fee-free visas. It is on the list where holders "can apply for a fee exemption". The ACT page states "If you are not eligible, you need to pay school tuition fees", and for a 482 exemption the "Main visa applicant must be working and living in the ACT".
facts.source: ACT Government, Enrol a child (dependant) of a temporary resident

facts.topic: Northern Territory NT school fees 482 visa
facts.text: The NT page says "To find out if you need to pay fees, select your child's visa below." Its "Working and skilled" table lists subclass 482 (Temporary skill shortage visa) with "Pay fees" marked "No".
facts.source: NT.GOV.AU, School fees for international students

facts.topic: NSW driving overseas licence 3 months permanent resident
facts.text: "If you're a permanent Australian resident, you'll need to get a NSW licence within 3 months to continue driving or riding."
facts.source: NSW Government, Moving your overseas licence to NSW

facts.topic: Victoria VIC driving overseas licence convert 6 months
facts.text: "If you're moving to Victoria and plan to live here for more than 6 months, you must convert" your overseas licence.
facts.source: VicRoads, Convert overseas licence

facts.topic: Western Australia WA driving overseas licence transfer 3 months
facts.text: Australian citizens and permanent residents can drive on a valid overseas licence for up to three months. "Within this 3-month period, you will need to apply to transfer your overseas driver's licence to a WA driver's licence."
facts.source: Transport WA, Moving from overseas

facts.topic: South Australia SA driving overseas licence 3 months
facts.text: Overseas licence holders must "get a South Australian driver's licence or permit within 3 months of becoming a permanent resident".
facts.source: SA.GOV.AU, Transfer your overseas driver's licence

facts.topic: ACT Canberra driving overseas licence permanent visa
facts.text: "Where you are the holder of, or are granted, a permanent visa you must obtain an ACT drivers licence."
facts.source: Access Canberra, Drivers with licences from overseas

facts.topic: Northern Territory NT driving overseas licence 3 months MVR
facts.text: "You must transfer your overseas driver licence or motorcycle licence within 3 months of living in the Northern Territory". You apply in person at an MVR office.
facts.source: NT.GOV.AU, Transfer your overseas driver licence

facts.topic: Powerswitch Consumer NZ not-for-profit power plans
facts.text: Powerswitch describes itself this way: "We're a not-for-profit, backed by Consumer NZ."
facts.source: Powerswitch, Compare and find cheap energy plans

facts.topic: Energy Made Easy coverage Australian Government Victoria WA NT
facts.text: "Energy Made Easy is a free Australian Government energy price comparison service." It covers "New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania and the Australian Capital Territory". Victoria is sent to Victorian Energy Compare, WA to the Economic Regulation Authority and the NT to Power and Water.
facts.source: Energy Made Easy (Australian Energy Regulator), Who can use Energy Made Easy?

facts.topic: Victoria VIC school fees 482 visa government school tuition free Melbourne
facts.text: Children of 482 visa holders do not pay tuition fees at Victorian government schools. This is Ethicare's own knowledge: the Department's International Student Visa Fee Table is not published, so families should confirm when they enrol.
facts.source: Ethicare (confirmed by Sophie Careem), with Study Victoria for enrolment

_directory_about: From 'Ask Ethicare — useful organisations and relocation directory' (6 Oct 2026). Commercial entries are options to compare, never recommendations or partners. Left out on purpose: the two commercial visa services (New Zealand Shores, Go Matilda Visas), because Ethicare does not name visa companies or advisers until it has a checked partnership (Sophie, 6 Oct 2026). Links were re-checked 12 Oct 2026 for the providers only where the original file had lost its links; recheck all entries quarterly.
